title: Maternal exposure to cyclophosphamide during prepubertal life does not affect the cryosusceptibility of in vitro derived mouse embryos.
ehr_evidence: Using a mouse model, this study evaluated the impact of prepubertal CY exposure (2 successive weekly doses of 75 mg/kg body weight at 2 weeks of age) on the cryosusceptibility of embryos derived via in vitro fertilization (IVF) at their reproductive phase.
summary: Experimental study using a prepubertal female Swiss albino mouse model to evaluate the impact of cyclophosphamide exposure on the cryosusceptibility, developmental competence, and pluripotency marker expression of in vitro derived embryos.
key_findings: Cyclophosphamide exposure caused a significant (P <0.0001) decline in total ovarian follicle count compared to controls.
Fertilization rates were comparable between control (84.3 ± 6.8) and CY (88.3 ± 4.9) groups.
Post-warming embryo survival rates were comparable between control (99.5 ± 0.5) and CY (99 ± 1) groups.

Blastocyst formation, apoptotic index, ICM outgrowth rates, and mRNA levels of Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog showed no significant differences between vitrified and non-vitrified CY embryos compared to controls.
captured_features: mRNA expression of Oct4, Sox2, Nanog
limitations: inability to assess in vivo implantation potential
restricted to a single chemotherapeutic agent and specific dosage
mouse model limitations for direct human translation
lack of direct dosage equivalence between mice and humans
